test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When the crank is at the dead centre, what will be the magnitude of bending moment and twisting moment at the crankshaft?

options.text: Both bending moment and twisting moment on the shaft are maximum
Both bending moment and the twisting moment are zero in the shaft
Bending moment on the shaft is maximum and the twisting moment is zero.
Bending moment on the shaft is minimum and the twisting moment is maximum.

solution:
The correct answer is __Bending moment on the shaft is maximum and the twisting moment is zero.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dead centre__ refers to the position of the crank when it is aligned with the connecting rod.
 
• At this position, the bending moment on the shaft is maximum.
 
• However, the twisting moment becomes zero in the shaft as there is no tangential force acting at the crank.
 
• This is a critical position in the analysis of mechanisms and crankshaft design.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Bending Moment:**

 
 
• It is the reaction induced in a structural element when an external force or moment is applied, causing the element to bend.
 
• In the crankshaft, the bending moment is dependent on the forces acting on the crank and the position of the crank.
 
 
 
• **Twisting Moment:**
 
 
• Also known as torque, it is the moment that causes an object to rotate about an axis.
 
• In the dead centre position, the tangential component of the force on the crank is zero, making the twisting moment zero.
